findings.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action is deliberately exempted from the login requirement (the diff adds :unsubscribe to the before_filter except-list at line 28, the same list that gates every other mutating action) but its body dereferences current_user.id, so an anonymous visitor reaches the action with current_user nil and crashes. A recipient who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link in a notification email while logged out — the primary flow this feature exists for — gets a 500 NoMethodError (undefined method `id' for nil:NilClass) instead of an unsubscribe page: TopicView.new succeeds for public topics, slugs match, then TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...) raises on nil.

[BUG] The shared unsubscribe_link translation gained a required %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation, but the diff supplies unsubscribe_url at only one call site (UserNotifications#send_notification_email), so every other Email::MessageBuilder caller that passes add_unsubscribe_link: true — the digest mailer — now builds template_args without it. Email::MessageBuilder#html_part evaluates I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for any email with add_unsubscribe_link: true regardless of whether its template even contains %{unsubscribe_link}, and the i18n gem raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument for the unbound %{unsubscribe_url} key, so digest emails fail to build and their sending jobs error instead of delivering.

[BUG] The template file registers under the name `topic/unsubscribe`, but the new route `topicUnsubscribe` (declared in routes/app-route-map.js.es6) resolves its default template through Ember's dasherized route-name lookup as `topic-unsubscribe`, a name this file location never produces. The template lookup misses and the route renders its resolved view (Discourse.TopicUnsubscribeView, which does resolve from the dasherized views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 — the sibling controller and view files follow the flat dasherized convention this template ignores) with no template, so the unsubscribe page shows the app shell with a blank content area and no way to change the notification level.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil for a logged-in user who has no topic_users row for the requested topic (e.g. someone other than the email recipient following the link, or a purged row), and the very next statement dereferences tu.notification_level. NoMethodError on nil → 500 instead of a 4xx; the TopicUser.change API used everywhere else in the codebase upserts the row and would have handled this case, while the direct find_by-then-mutate pattern turns any missing row into a server error.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe controller action ships with no spec in this diff despite containing branching logic (slug-canonicalization redirect, notification-level toggle) and two nil-deref hazards. The anonymous-500 and nil-row-500 failure modes and the toggle direction (watching/tracking → regular on first click, muted only on a second click) are all untested, so a regression in the action — the one piece of this feature that mutates user data — ships silently; the only test added covers Email::MessageBuilder, not this endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` and the template binds the identical misspelling ({{{stopNotificiationsText}}}), so the pair only works while both halves stay wrong. A routine spelling fix in either file alone silently breaks the binding — the property becomes undefined, the triple-stache renders an empty paragraph, and the page's main message ('You will stop receiving notifications for …') disappears with no error to flag it.

[ADVISORY] The action mutates and saves the TopicUser row directly instead of going through TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus.publish('/topic/:id', {notification_level_change: ...}, user_ids: [user_id]) that TopicUser.change performs (visible in the topic_user.rb changes in this same diff). The user's other open browser sessions never receive the notification_level_change message and keep displaying the old tracking/watching state for the topic until a full reload, diverging from every other notification-level change path in the app.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe routes perform a state-changing write on GET with check_xhr skipped for the action and no token in the URL, making the mutation triggerable by any cross-site embed. A logged-in user who loads an attacker-controlled page containing gets their notification level for that topic toggled with no interaction (the browser sends session cookies on the image request; two loads mutes the topic), unlike every other notification-level change which goes through the CSRF-protected PUT /t/:id/notifications endpoint.

[BUG] The shared `unsubscribe_link` locale string now requires the %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation, but the diff supplies it at only one call site (UserNotifications#send_notification_email, user_notifications.rb:295) — every other email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g. UserNotifications.digest, whose template renders the same %{unsubscribe_link} footer through Email::MessageBuilder#html_part) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at message_builder.rb:67. Digest (and any other add_unsubscribe_link) email builds raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, so the background mail jobs fail and those emails stop being delivered entirely; the in-diff spec change (message_builder_spec.rb:171) had to add unsubscribe_url to the existing fixture just to keep passing, which confirms the argument is now mandatory for every consumer of this string.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences tu.notification_level with no nil guard after TopicUser.find_by, so a logged-in user with no topic_users row for that topic gets a NoMethodError 500. Anyone clicking a forwarded or shared unsubscribe link while logged into their own account (their TopicUser row for the topic does not exist) gets a 500 error page instead of an unsubscribe or a 404; the action has no fallback path.

[BUG] tu.notification_level can be NULL — track_visit! creates topic_users rows without a notification_level (topic_user.rb:126) and the tracking scope in the same file COALESCEs the column against :regular precisely because it is nullable — so `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` raises ArgumentError (comparison of NilClass with Integer failed) and returns a 500. A logged-in user whose topic_users row was created by track_visit! with a NULL notification_level gets a 500 when clicking the emailed unsubscribe link, the feature's primary flow.

[BUG] The action ratchets the notification level down one step (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted) instead of muting, so a watching or tracking user who clicks the link promising "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>" is left at regular and continues to receive notification emails for that topic; and because the mutation runs on every GET, merely opening or refreshing the unsubscribe URL silently steps the user's level down. Watching/tracking users keep getting emails after clicking "stop notifications" (the copy in server.en.yml:1855 and client.en.yml contradicts the behavior), and a logged-in user who opens the page out of curiosity or from browser history is muted without intending to be.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with check_xhr skipped and no user-binding token in the URL, so a cross-site — the 301 slug redirect completes the request even without the slug — flips the notification level of any logged-in visitor, and whoever clicks a forwarded link changes their own account's settings, not the recipient's. Any third-party web page can silently mute topics for a logged-in user via CSRF (Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and check_xhr was the guard being removed); forwarded emails unsubscribe the wrong account.

[ADVISORY] The action assigns tu.notification_level and calls save! directly instead of going through TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...}) that every other notification-level change performs (topic_user.rb:113). The user's other open browsers/tabs never receive the live notification_level_change message and keep showing and acting on the stale level; the change also creates a second hand-maintained path for level mutations that must be kept in sync with TopicUser.change's bookkeeping.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` (the template unsubscribe.hbs:3 references the same misspelling, so it renders today, but the shipped identifier is wrong in both places). The next maintainer who references the correctly-spelled stopNotificationsText — or greps the codebase for 'Notifications' — gets undefined and ships a blank paragraph; the typo is now duplicated across the controller and template, doubling the fix surface.

[ADVISORY] The only test touched patches the existing fixture to pass unsubscribe_url; no test in the diff renders an add_unsubscribe_link email WITHOUT unsubscribe_url (the exact regression class that breaks digest), and TopicsController#unsubscribe — slug redirect, level ratchet, nil-row and nil-level paths — has no spec anywhere in the diff. The digest-breaking interpolation regression and the controller's 500 paths ship unverified; any later refactor of the toggle logic or the unsubscribe_link string has no safety net and re-breaks email delivery silently.

[ADVISORY] The action is added to the login-gated before_filter list (alongside bookmark/invite/bulk), so a user clicking the emailed link in a browser without an active session is bounced before the action runs and the unsubscribe is never performed; the diff contains no magic-token or return-to handling for this case. The feature's primary entry point — clicking the link in the email — requires an existing forum session; logged-out users (email opened on a phone or another device) hit the auth wall first, and whether they ever land back on the unsubscribe page depends on login destination handling outside this diff.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe calls tu.notification_level with no nil guard after TopicUser.find_by, so a recipient with no TopicUser row for the topic gets NoMethodError and a 500. A user mentioned in (or quoted in) a topic they have never opened has no TopicUser record; clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link in exactly that email — the primary flow this feature ships for — raises NoMethodError (undefined method `notification_level` for nil) and renders a 500 instead of unsubscribing.

[BUG] The comparison tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] crashes with NoMethodError (undefined method `>` for nil) when the TopicUser row has a nil notification_level. TopicUser rows created by track_visit! (app/models/topic_user.rb:125 in this diff) are created without a notification_level attribute, and the tracking scope's COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular) in the same file exists precisely because nil-level rows occur; a user whose only row came from a visit gets a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page.

[BUG] The shared unsubscribe_link translation gained a required %{unsubscribe_url} placeholder, but only the send_notification_email call site was updated to supply it, so Email::MessageBuilder#html_part's I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument for any other email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g. digest and private-message notification emails in user_notifications.rb). Every affected email fails to build and is never sent; the in-diff spec change proves the argument is now mandatory — message_builder_spec.rb had to add unsubscribe_url to message_with_unsubscribe or the existing test fails, and no other production call site in the diff receives the new opt.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action performs a non-idempotent state mutation (watching→regular→muted on each repeated GET) on a plain GET endpoint with no confirmation step and no CSRF protection (Rails does not token-verify GET). Email link-scanning gateways (Outlook SafeLinks, corporate mail filters) that prefetch links, a double-click, or a cross-site embedded in any webpage silently demote/mute the logged-in user's topic subscription without consent; repeated invocations keep demoting until muted.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser row directly via tu.save! instead of going through TopicUser.change, bypassing the MessageBus notification_level_change publish that every other notification-level write path in topic_user.rb performs. The user's other open tabs/clients never receive the /topic/:id message and show stale subscription state, and a second write path now exists that future side-effects centralized in TopicUser.change will not cover — using TopicUser.change would also have handled the missing-row case that crashes this action.

[ADVISORY] The new state-changing unsubscribe action — nil handling, the notification-level toggle, and the slug-mismatch redirect — has zero test coverage in this diff; the only spec touched is message_builder_spec.rb, updated only because the new constructor argument became mandatory. Regressions in the toggle logic or the nil-row crash ship undetected; the nil-TopicUser 500 in this same action is exactly the class of bug a minimal controller spec would have caught.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText ('Notificiations') in the controller, and the unsubscribe template references the same misspelled name. It works today only because both sides share the typo; the next maintainer grepping for 'notifications' or renaming one side silently breaks the page's headline text.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe link acts on current_user (the browser session) rather than on the email recipient — the URL carries no recipient-bound token. If the notification email is forwarded, or read on a machine where a different user is logged into the same Discourse, clicking 'stop notifications about this particular topic' mutes the wrong user's subscription for that topic.

[ADVISORY] The diff drops the post_number: /\d+/ constraint from both /summary routes (lines 439 and 442), a behavioral change to summary routing with no traceable connection to the per-topic unsubscribe feature. Reviewers of an unsubscribe PR must now validate summary-route matching; if the constraint was load-bearing, which URLs match the summary routes changes with no test and no mention in the commit intent.

[ADVISORY] topic_user.rb carries roughly six hunks of pure reformatting (tracking scope indentation, create_lookup compaction, MessageBus.publish argument layout, hash-rocket to kwargs in track_visit!) that are unrelated to the unsubscribe feature. The feature diff balloons across a core model, git blame on topic_user.rb is polluted, and a real behavior change could hide inside the reformat during review.

[ADVISORY] The core topic-loading route is wholesale restyled (var→const, function(){}→method shorthand, self hoisted into the const declaration) with no behavior change, unrelated to per-topic unsubscribe. Churn in a hot, core route inflates the diff a reviewer must audit line-by-line and risks a regression in topic loading hiding inside an ostensibly cosmetic hunk.

[ADVISORY] notification.html.erb is fully reindented and restructured with identical logic — the only feature-relevant line is the already-existing %{unsubscribe_link} footer div. The email template diff is dominated by whitespace churn (footer divs collapse to single lines, changing emitted email HTML whitespace), making it hard to audit the actual feature change in the email pipeline.

[ADVISORY] message_builder.rb's changes are reformat-only (template_args hash layout here, the respond_instructions assignment and gsub spacing further down) with no behavior change, despite touching the exact code that renders the new unsubscribe link. The substantive change — unsubscribe_url becoming a required template argument — is buried inside reformatting, so reviewers auditing this file for the feature's contract change must diff cosmetic hunks first.

[ADVISORY] The confirmation copy 'You will stop receiving notifications for X' is rendered unconditionally, but a watching/tracking user is only demoted to regular, which still produces mention and reply-to-your-post emails for that topic. A user clicking the link from a mention email — the email that likely brought them there — believes they opted out but keeps receiving emails about the topic until they click a second time (regular→muted).

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences `tu` with no nil guard: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil for any logged-in user who has no TopicUser row for the topic, and the very next statement calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError. A logged-in user who opens an unsubscribe link from a forwarded notification email (or hand-types /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe) for a topic they never interacted with gets a 500 error page instead of unsubscribing; the same block also crashes with ArgumentError (`nil > 1`) for rows whose notification_level is nil, a state this diff's own code acknowledges — TopicUser.tracking wraps the column in COALESCE and track_visit! creates rows without setting notification_level.

[BUG] The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires the %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to supply it — every other email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true renders I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') from Email::MessageBuilder#html_part with template_args that contain no unsubscribe_url. Rendering any such email raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument inside MessageBuilder, so the email build fails and it is never sent (the Sidekiq mail job errors instead of delivering); the diff itself confirms the key is mandatory at render time — the message_builder_spec fixture had to gain unsubscribe_url for the existing examples to keep passing.

[BUG] The unsubscribe endpoint performs a persistent state change on a plain GET request (check_xhr is skipped for it and no confirmation step or token exists), and the action is not idempotent — each invocation steps the notification level further down (watching/tracking → regular → muted). Mail-client link prefetchers and corporate URL scanners (e.g., Outlook SafeLinks, which GET every link in delivered mail) will silently mute the recipient's topic without any user action, so users stop receiving notification emails they never asked to turn off; the state change is also reachable by any third party embedding the URL in an image tag on a page the user visits while logged in.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates TopicUser.notification_level via find_by + save! instead of going through the canonical TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...}, user_ids: [user_id]) that TopicUser.change performs on every notification-level mutation — the publish is visible in this same diff inside topic_user.rb. The user's other open tabs/sessions subscribed to /topic/:id never receive the notification_level_change message and show a stale notification state after unsubscribing; this second, parallel mutation path for notification levels also means any logic later added to TopicUser.change (reason tracking, side effects) is silently bypassed by this action.

[BUG] For users at tracking or watching level the action downgrades to :regular instead of :muted, so one click on the email link does not stop topic notifications, contradicting the copy this diff adds ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}'). A tracking/watching user who clicks the unsubscribe link keeps receiving reply/mention emails for that topic while the confirmation page asserts notifications have stopped, producing repeat clicks and support confusion; only a second invocation (regular → muted) fulfills the promise the email made.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences `tu.notification_level` with no guard for a missing topic_users row or a NULL notification_level, so `nil > 0` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s. A user whose topic_users row was created by track_visit! (which, in this same diff, inserts rows without notification_level) or by the email-send TopicUser.change call has notification_level = NULL — the tracking scope's COALESCE(notification_level, :regular) exists precisely because NULL levels occur — and clicking the new email link throws NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing; a nil row (e.g., link clicked for a topic the user never interacted with) fails the same way, so the feature's primary action hard-fails for a real subset of recipients.

[BUG] The notification-level mutation is performed inside a GET request, which Rails never CSRF-checks, so any authenticated cross-site request to the URL executes the unsubscribe. An attacker page containing silently mutes topic 123 for every logged-in visitor whose browser sends the session cookie (2015-era cookies are sent on cross-site GETs); the mute is applied server-side before any page renders, so the victim receives no confirmation and simply stops receiving notifications for topics they never opted out of.

[BUG] The action downgrades one notification level instead of muting, so tracking users — the typical recipients, since replying auto-sets tracking — are set to regular and keep receiving reply/mention emails for the topic. The email footer promises "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" and the confirmation page says "You will stop receiving notifications for …", but a tracking user who clicks continues to receive reply and mention emails for that topic (regular level still produces them), so the feature's user-visible contract is false for its primary audience and only repeated clicks eventually reach muted.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but html_part renders it unconditionally for every email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true and only send_notification_email was updated to pass the argument. Any other Email::MessageBuilder caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without passing unsubscribe_url (digest/PM/plugin builders — the spec change proves the old builder options now raise) gets I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time, so those emails fail to send; the interpolation contract of a shared email path was changed silently with a single call site updated.

[ADVISORY] The shared dropdown-button component's rendered output changed (the <h4 class='title'> is now omitted when title is blank), an unrequested behavior change to every existing usage bundled into this feature. Existing dropdown-button instances that render with a blank title previously emitted an empty heading (contributing default h4 margins/spacing) and now emit nothing, so pages other than the new unsubscribe screen can shift layout; no audit of other usages accompanies the change.

[ADVISORY] The feature diff carries wholesale non-functional churn — topic_user.rb reformatting across five hunks, message_builder.rb and notification.html.erb reindentation, and routes.rb line reordering that silently drops the summary routes' post_number constraint. Reviewers and future archaeologists cannot distinguish intentional from accidental changes in this diff (the dropped post_number constraint happens to be inert because the path has no :post_number segment, but nothing in the diff says so), and any real regression hiding in the reformatting is effectively unreviewable.

[ADVISORY] The new state-mutating unsubscribe action — with level-comparison branching, a 301 redirect path, and an unguarded nil dereference — ships with zero test coverage. The only spec touched is message_builder_spec; a regression in the toggle logic, the slug-mismatch redirect, or the nil crash (finding above) ships silently, and the exact class of bug the action already contains is precisely what a controller spec would have caught before merge.

[ADVISORY] tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so no /topic/:id MessageBus notification_level_change message is published for the user. The user's other open sessions (e.g., the topic open in another tab — likely, since they arrived from an email about it) keep showing the stale notification state and watching indicators until a full reload; TopicUser.change exists precisely to centralize create-or-update plus this publish, and the action hand-rolls a divergent copy of it.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText`, and the template binds the same misspelling via {{{stopNotificiationsText}}}. It works today only because both sides share the typo; the next developer who corrects the spelling in either file silently renders an empty

on the unsubscribe page (Handlebars resolves the missing property to nothing) with no error pointing at the mismatch.

[BUG] The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires a %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation argument, but Email::MessageBuilder#html_part (lib/email/message_builder.rb, the `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` line) runs for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url` — every other such email raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time. Any notification email other than post-notification emails that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g., private-message notification emails, digest mail) now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the message is built, so those emails are never delivered and the sending job errors; the diff's own spec change (adding unsubscribe_url to message_with_unsubscribe) confirms the argument is now mandatory for the builder, and no default is added in Email::MessageBuilder#initialize.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the current user has no topic_users row for the topic (e.g., a user mentioned in a topic they never opened, or anyone opening a forwarded unsubscribe link), and the immediately following `tu.notification_level` dereference raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of an unsubscribe. Clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link that this PR adds to notification emails returns a 500 error page instead of unsubscribing whenever the recipient has no TopicUser record for that topic — the feature's primary click-through fails for exactly the casual recipients it targets — and any logged-in user can trigger the same 500 by GETting /t/<id>/unsubscribe for any topic they can view but have never interacted with.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a state change (tu.save! flipping notification_level) on a GET request, with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 32) removing the XHR-header guard and Rails' protect_from_forgery exempting GET, so no authenticity token or non-GET verb is required to mutate a user's notification preferences. A cross-site top-level link (or an /prefetch on browsers without SameSite=Lax defaults, plus email-client link prefetchers) fires /t//unsubscribe with the victim's session and silently mutes or downgrades their notifications for any sequential topic id without any user intent or CSRF token — an attacker page or a mail client's prefetcher can suppress a user's topic notifications at scale.

[BUG] The diff's only test change feeds the new unsubscribe_url option into the MessageBuilder fixture while the sole assertion it feeds (header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present) never reads that option, making the test change inert with respect to the feature it exists to verify. The suite stays green if the per-topic unsubscribe link never renders in any email: nothing asserts that %{unsubscribe_url} (config/locales/server.en.yml:1854) is interpolated into html_part (lib/email/message_builder.rb:66-69), that Topic#unsubscribe_url (app/models/topic.rb:719-721) produces a usable URL, or that user_notifications.rb:295 passes it through. The fixture's hand-typed relative '/t/1234/unsubscribe' bypasses the real producer (so a wrong URL shape ships undetected), and the fixture has no html_override, so html_part — the only code that substitutes the link — is never even exercised. No pre-existing test could have covered this either, since the option is introduced in this PR.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe action's branches — the 301 slug-mismatch/blank-slug redirect (lines 101-103), both notification_level toggle directions (lines 107-111), and tu.save! — have zero spec coverage; the only test file in this diff (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) references only Email::MessageBuilder and never this controller. The feature's server-side core can regress with CI green: nothing verifies that clicking the email link actually downgrades the user's notification level to muted (or what a second click does), nor that the slug-normalization redirect fires, nor that the new routes in config/routes.rb resolve to this action — a broken unsubscribe flow for every email recipient reaches production silently.

[BUG] unsubscribe dereferences tu.notification_level on the result of TopicUser.find_by with no nil guard and compares it with >, so it raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 when the clicking user has no TopicUser row (e.g. a forwarded notification email opened by another logged-in user) or when notification_level is NULL — a state this diff's own tracking scope explicitly handles via COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular) at app/models/topic_user.rb:9. A logged-in user clicking the email's per-topic unsubscribe link gets a Rails 500 instead of being unsubscribed; the branch is untested (no spec in the diff touches this action), so the crash ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The new Ember route (model hook with store.createRecord + PostStream.loadTopicView + updateFromJson, afterModel's notificationReasonText nulling, didTransition footer toggle), its controller, and the unsubscribe template ship with no JS test anywhere in the diff. The page every email recipient lands on after clicking the unsubscribe link can regress silently — a loadTopicView failure or an updateFromJson payload-shape change renders a blank or broken page with no failing test; absence verified against the diff's only test file, spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb, which references Email::MessageBuilder and no frontend symbol.

[ADVISORY] perform_show_response — shared with the existing show action — now explicitly renders :show inside the format.html block (added so unsubscribe can reuse it), modifying the main topic-show rendering path with no test in the diff covering the HTML response of either caller. A regression in the site's highest-traffic page's rendering ships with CI green, and the next change to perform_show_response must now stay correct for two callers with different parameter contexts (show vs. unsubscribe) with nothing guarding either.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText ('Notificiations') and the template (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3) repeats the identical misspelling, so rendering works only while both hand-maintained sides share the typo. The next edit that corrects the spelling on one side only (a rename or a copy-paste of the 'obvious' correct name) silently renders an empty paragraph on the unsubscribe page, and no test exists to catch it.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by without a nil check, so any logged-in user who has no TopicUser row for the topic crashes with NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and gets a raw 500 instead of a graceful page. A logged-in user who is not the email recipient (different account on a shared machine clicking the emailed link, or anyone navigating directly to /t/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they never interacted with) hits a 500 error page; TopicUser.find_by returns nil because a TopicUser row is only guaranteed for the recipient (created by TopicUser.change at email-send time), and the canonical TopicUser.change API — which creates the missing row — is exactly what this action bypasses.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates TopicUser directly via tu.save! instead of going through TopicUser.change, so the MessageBus '/topic/:id' notification_level_change message that every other notification-level change publishes (TopicUser.change and update_last_read both publish it) is never sent. A user with the topic open in another tab or browser keeps displaying the stale notification level there until a full reload, and any client logic keyed on the notification_level_change MessageBus message silently misses the change; the established pattern in topic_user.rb for this exact mutation is bypassed.

[ADVISORY] The route model hook returns PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...) with no rejection handler, so a failed topic fetch aborts the transition with no error surface — even though the server already performed the unsubscribe mutation during the initial HTML GET. A user clicking the email link on a flaky connection (or hitting the window where the topic becomes invisible between the server render and the Ember fetch) lands on a blank/stuck page with no confirmation and no error message, while their notification level has already been changed; the user cannot tell the operation succeeded.

[ADVISORY] The one-level toggle (watching/tracking -> regular, regular/muted -> muted) does not deliver what the copy promises ('You will stop receiving notifications for X' / 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic'): a tracking user downgraded to regular keeps receiving the same reply/mention emails, and a watching user keeps receiving reply emails. Users click 'stop notifications about this topic', see a confirmation that notifications will stop, and keep getting emails for that topic, so the feature silently under-delivers on its primary path; additionally the toggle is not idempotent — merely reloading the confirmation page downgrades the level again (regular -> muted) — so the resulting state depends on how many times the page was loaded.

[ADVISORY] The new topics#unsubscribe action — a state-mutating GET with slug-redirect logic, toggle semantics, and an unchecked find_by — ships with no test coverage in this diff; the only spec change is the message_builder fixture. A regression in the toggle constants, the slug-canonicalization redirect, or the nil handling would silently break per-topic unsubscribing for all users with no failing test; the nil-deref 500 in this action is precisely the kind of edge case a controller spec for the new endpoint would have surfaced before merge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] unsubscribe dereferences tu.notification_level on the result of TopicUser.find_by with no nil guard and compares it with >, so it raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 when the clicking user has no TopicUser row (e.g. a forwarded notification email opened by another logged-in user) or when notification_level is NULL — a state this diff's own tracking scope explicitly handles via COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular) at app/models/topic_user.rb:9. A logged-in user clicking the email's per-topic unsubscribe link gets a Rails 500 instead of being unsubscribed; the branch is untested (no spec in the diff touches this action), so the crash ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it: `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` and later `tu.save!`. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, `tu` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Even if `tu` exists but `notification_level` is `NULL`, `nil > <integer>` will also raise. The diff itself shows `TopicUser` scopes handle `NULL` via `COALESCE(...)` (so `NULL` is plausible), but the new controller action does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by without a nil check, so any logged-in user who has no TopicUser row for the topic crashes with NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and gets a raw 500 instead of a graceful page. A logged-in user who is not the email recipient (different account on a shared machine clicking the emailed link, or anyone navigating directly to /t/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they never interacted with) hits a 500 error page; TopicUser.find_by returns nil because a TopicUser row is only guaranteed for the recipient (created by TopicUser.change at email-send time), and the canonical TopicUser.change API — which creates the missing row — is exactly what this action bypasses.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level`, then assigns and `tu.save!`) with no nil handling. From the diff alone, `find_by` can return `nil` for a logged-in user who has no `TopicUser` row for that topic, which would raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500. The action also bypasses the existing `TopicUser.change(...)` API (shown elsewhere in the diff) that would create a missing row, reinforcing the crash scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates TopicUser directly via tu.save! instead of going through TopicUser.change, so the MessageBus '/topic/:id' notification_level_change message that every other notification-level change publishes (TopicUser.change and update_last_read both publish it) is never sent. A user with the topic open in another tab or browser keeps displaying the stale notification level there until a full reload, and any client logic keyed on the notification_level_change MessageBus message silently misses the change; the established pattern in topic_user.rb for this exact mutation is bypassed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!` (no call to `TopicUser.change`). In the same diff, `TopicUser.change` clearly publishes a MessageBus event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). Since `unsubscribe` bypasses this path and does not publish any MessageBus message itself, the `notification_level_change` event will not be emitted for this change, unlike other notification-level mutations shown in `topic_user.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The route model hook returns PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...) with no rejection handler, so a failed topic fetch aborts the transition with no error surface — even though the server already performed the unsubscribe mutation during the initial HTML GET. A user clicking the email link on a flaky connection (or hitting the window where the topic becomes invisible between the server render and the Ember fetch) lands on a blank/stuck page with no confirmation and no error message, while their notification level has already been changed; the user cannot tell the operation succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` has `model(params) { ... return PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...) }` with no `.catch(...)` / error action shown in the diff. In Ember, a rejected model-hook promise will abort the transition unless an error substate/action handles it; this diff doesn’t add any such handling for this route. At the same time, the server-side `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (new in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`) performs the notification-level mutation (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) during the initial GET before rendering. So a failed client fetch after the mutation is a real “changed state but no confirmation UI” failure mode introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The one-level toggle (watching/tracking -> regular, regular/muted -> muted) does not deliver what the copy promises ('You will stop receiving notifications for X' / 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic'): a tracking user downgraded to regular keeps receiving the same reply/mention emails, and a watching user keeps receiving reply emails. Users click 'stop notifications about this topic', see a confirmation that notifications will stop, and keep getting emails for that topic, so the feature silently under-delivers on its primary path; additionally the toggle is not idempotent — merely reloading the confirmation page downgrades the level again (regular -> muted) — so the resulting state depends on how many times the page was loaded.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the link performs a GET that mutates state by toggling `TopicUser#notification_level` (`> regular` => set to `regular`, else set to `muted`). This is (a) not idempotent: a user at `regular` will be changed to `muted` simply by reloading the unsubscribe URL, so the resulting state depends on how many times the page is loaded; and (b) it does not necessarily “stop receiving notifications” as the copy claims, because users at `watching`/`tracking` are only downgraded to `regular`, not forced to `muted` (`Topic#unsubscribe_url` + server locale text promise “stop receiving notifications about this particular topic”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new topics#unsubscribe action — a state-mutating GET with slug-redirect logic, toggle semantics, and an unchecked find_by — ships with no test coverage in this diff; the only spec change is the message_builder fixture. A regression in the toggle constants, the slug-canonicalization redirect, or the nil handling would silently break per-topic unsubscribing for all users with no failing test; the nil-deref 500 in this action is precisely the kind of edge case a controller spec for the new endpoint would have surfaced before merge.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` is not checked for nil before dereferencing: `tu.notification_level > ...` and later `tu.save!`. If no `TopicUser` row exists for the current user/topic, this will raise (500) — a concrete defect visible in the diff. The action also mutates notification state via a GET route (`get ... => topics#unsubscribe`), but the nil-deref alone makes this a verifiable bug introduced by the change; the lack of endpoint test coverage in this diff further increases regression risk but is secondary.
